item.text:
{"program":"domain(person,[bria]).

% If Bria either turns trash into treasure or makes something useful (but not both), then she creates something valuable.
axiom(s1, rule([xor(turns_trash_into_treasure(bria), makes_something_useful(bria))], creates_something_valuable(bria))).

% Bria creates something valuable or solves problems.
axiom(s2, or(creates_something_valuable(bria), solves_problems(bria))).

% For all persons, if they are curious and try new things, then they enjoy experimenting.
axiom(s3, rule([curious(X), try_new_things(X)], enjoy_experimenting(X))).

% If Bria has imagination, then she will try new things.
axiom(s4, rule([has_imagination(bria)], try_new_things(bria))).

% For all people, if a person is creative, then they think outside the box and create something valuable.
axiom(s5, rule([creative(X)], and(thinks_outside_the_box(X), creates_something_valuable(X)))).

% Bria does not achieve success.
axiom(s6, not(achieves_success(bria))).

% Bria is innovative.
axiom(s7, innovative(bria)).

% If someone is innovative and enjoys experimenting, then they are creative.
axiom(s8, rule([innovative(X), enjoy_experimenting(X)], creative(X))).

% Bria has imagination.
axiom(s9, has_imagination(bria)).

% Anyone who loves learning and solves problems can achieve success.
axiom(s10, rule([loves_learning(X), solves_problems(X)], achieves_success(X))).

% Bria loves learning.
axiom(s11, loves_learning(bria)).

% Bria is curious.
axiom(s12, curious(bria)).","query":"labelled_explanation(thinks_outside_the_box(bria), Status, Package)"}
